mainTopic: Does halacha follow the Torah's reading (יש אם למקרא) or its spelling (יש אם למסורת)? The גמרא tests both views against earlier disputes and against the ruling of בשר בחלב.
overview: This amud asks whether halacha follows the way the Torah is read aloud (יש אם למקרא) or the way it is written (יש אם למסורת). It opens by finishing a proof from בשר בחלב: everyone reads חלב as 'milk', so everyone seems to follow the reading. The גמרא then re-explains five earlier disputes so that none of them depends on reading versus writing. These are רבי and רבנן on judges, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית הלל on חטאת blood, the סוכה walls, and blood from two dead bodies. For בית הלל it quotes a ברייתא where two logical comparisons cancel out, so the threefold 'וכפר' teaches that even one placement of blood atones. Next a ברייתא about טוטפות shows that רבי ישמעאל does follow the spelling, so the תנאים really do argue. The גמרא first limits the argument to cases where reading and spelling differ. The case of יראה/יראה knocks down that limit. Finally רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains the milk ruling from the word 'cook', since cooking is done in a liquid. The amud ends by opening a new ברייתא saying monetary cases need three judges.

steps.title: Finishing the proof: everyone follows the reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the proof from בשר בחלב: since we read 'חלב' as milk and not as fat, we clearly follow the way the Torah is read aloud. Step 14 later narrows this proof, and step 17 replaces it with a different reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: So you are forced to say: the way the Torah is read aloud is the authority.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a proof that started just before this section. Because everyone forbids cooking a kid in its mother's milk, everyone must agree that the reading decides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without vowels, the letters חלב could be read as 'fat' instead of 'milk'. Nobody actually holds that the verse is talking about fat, so for now the גמרא concludes that all opinions follow the reading aloud. This undercuts the earlier idea that some of the תנאים follow only the written letters (יש אם למסורת).

keyTerms.meaning: The way the Torah is read aloud (with its vowels) is the authority for learning הלכה
The way the Torah is written (its letters, without vowels) is the authority
You must say, meaning you are forced to admit

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of an argument, not the start of a new one. The case it relies on (בשר בחלב) came just before this section.

phrases.english: You must say: the reading is the authority.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק about cooking a kid in its mother's חלב. The letters could also be read as 'fat', but we read them as 'milk'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof from בשר בחלב that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That every opinion holds יש אם למקרא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse 'לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו', which everyone reads as milk and not as fat.

steps.title: New explanation of the argument between רבי and רבנן
steps.stepSummary: Since everyone holds יש אם למקרא, the argument between רבי and רבנן about the number of judges must be about something else: whether 'ירשיעון אלהים' adds new judges or refers back to the same ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees the reading is the authority. רבי and רבנן argue about this point: רבי holds that 'the judges shall condemn' means additional judges, while רבנן hold that 'shall condemn' means the same judges already mentioned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason for the argument between רבי and רבנן. It is not about reading versus writing anymore; it is about what one phrase in the verse means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says 'ירשיעון אלהים' brings in two more judges beyond the three already counted, which makes five. רבנן say the phrase only describes the same judges who were already counted, which leaves three. Both sides read the word the same way; they differ on whether it adds people.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
They argue about
'The judges shall condemn' (a phrase in the verse about monetary cases)
Others, meaning additional judges
Of those and these, meaning the same judges already mentioned

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the pattern for the rest of the section: once יש אם למקרא is accepted by all, each earlier dispute must be explained some other way.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא,
phrases.english: Rather, everyone holds the reading is the authority,
and Rabbi and the Rabbis argue about this:
Rabbi holds that "the judges shall condemn" means other judges,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8. These 'other' judges are added to the three already counted, which gives five.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold that "shall condemn" refers to those same ones.
phrases.notes: In other words, no new judges are added, so the court stays at three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the proof in step 1 to give a new explanation of the dispute between רבי and רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the basis of the dispute from reading versus writing to what the phrase means.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי holds יש אם למקרא and רבנן hold יש אם למסורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold יש אם למקרא. They argue over whether 'ירשיעון אלהים' adds new judges (five) or refers back to the same ones (three).

steps.title: רבנן do not argue with רבי יהודה בן רועץ
steps.stepSummary: The ruling of רבי יהודה בן רועץ, which is based on how a word is read aloud, is not actually disputed by רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי יהודה בן רועץ, the Rabbis do not disagree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא deals with the next earlier opinion. It says that רבי יהודה בן רועץ's use of the reading is accepted by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it looked as if רבנן disagreed with רבי יהודה בן רועץ because they followed the written letters. Now that everyone holds יש אם למקרא, the גמרא simply says there is no disagreement here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who learned a law about a woman who gave birth to a girl from the way a word is read aloud
They do not disagree

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda ben Roetz,
the Rabbis do not disagree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן רוֹעֵץ, לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the earlier list of opinions, now dealing with רבי יהודה בן רועץ.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבנן disagree with רבי יהודה בן רועץ because they follow the written letters.
steps.terutzMaskana: No one disagrees, because everyone follows the reading.

steps.title: בית הלל's source is a ברייתא about 'וכפר'
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל's ruling about the blood of a חטאת does not come from following the written letters. It comes from a ברייתא that explains why the Torah says 'וכפר' three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for בית הלל, their ruling comes from what was taught in a ברייתא: 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone,' 'and he shall atone.' This repetition is because of a logical argument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different source for בית הלל and begins quoting a ברייתא. This step is setup: steps 5-9 spell out the logical argument the ברייתא mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it seemed that בית הלל hold one placement of blood is enough because they follow the written letters. Now the גמרא says they learn it from the three times the Torah repeats 'וכפר'. The ברייתא says this repetition was needed to block a logical argument, and that argument comes right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, who hold that one placement of blood is enough for a חטאת
As was taught in a ברייתא
And he (the כהן) shall atone
Because of a logical argument (that the extra words come to block)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. 'מפני הדין' only opens the logical argument, which steps 5-9 lay out.

phrases.english: As for Beit Hillel, it is as was taught:
"And he shall atone," "and he shall atone," "and he shall atone" – this is because of a logical argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the earlier opinions, now giving בית הלל a source other than the written letters.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different source for the same ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל rule that one placement is enough because they hold יש אם למסורת.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל learn their ruling from the threefold 'וכפר' in a ברייתא, not from reading versus writing.

steps.title: Logic suggests one placement of blood is enough, learned from the bird offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests we could work out by logic that one placement of blood atones for an animal חטאת. It learns this from the bird חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Couldn't we figure this out by logic? The Torah mentions 'blood' below, for the bird חטאת, and 'blood' above, for the animal חטאת. A bird's blood placed once atones. So the animal's blood placed once should also atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether we even need a פסוק. It tries to prove from the bird חטאת that one placement of blood is enough for an animal חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת has its blood placed low on the מזבח, and one placement is enough. The animal חטאת has its blood placed up high on the corners. Since both use the word 'blood', the ברייתא suggests the animal follows the bird: one placement atones.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it logical? This opens an attempt to learn a law by reasoning instead of from a פסוק.
A placement of blood on the מזבח.
It has atoned, meaning the offering did its job.
Below or above, meaning the lower or upper part of the מזבח.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Below' and 'above' here do not mean lower or higher in the פסוק. They mean where the blood goes on the מזבח: low for the bird, up on the corners for the animal.

phrases.english: But isn't it logical?
"Blood" is stated below,
phrases.notes: This is the bird חטאת, whose blood goes on the lower part of the מזבח (ויקרא 5:9).

phrases.english: and "blood" is stated above.
phrases.notes: This is the animal חטאת, whose blood goes up on the corners (ויקרא 4:25).

phrases.english: Just as with the blood stated below,
if one placed it with one placement, it atoned,
so too with the blood stated above,
if one placed it with one placement, it atoned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא introduced in Step 4. It tries logic before relying on the triple 'וכפר'.
steps.raayaObject: One placement of blood atones for an animal חטאת on the outer מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to the bird חטאת, where one placement of blood is enough.

steps.title: A rival comparison: learn from the inner offerings, where missing one placement ruins everything
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers the opposite comparison. Learn the outer חטאת from the inner חטאת, where missing even one placement makes the offering worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: 'blood' is said about the outer מזבח and about the inner one. Inside, if one placement is missing, nothing was done. So outside too, if one placement is missing, nothing was done.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back on the first idea with a different comparison that leads to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner offerings have their blood placed inside the היכל, and every single placement is required. If the outer חטאת is compared to them, then all its placements are needed too, and one is not enough. Now there are two comparisons that point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way. This introduces a rival line of reasoning.
Outside, meaning the outer מזבח in the courtyard.
Inside, meaning the inner, golden מזבח in the היכל.
He did nothing, meaning the offering is invalid.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
"Blood" is stated regarding outside,
and "blood" is stated regarding inside.
phrases.notes: The חטאת of the כהן גדול or the community, whose blood goes on the inner מזבח (ויקרא 4:7, 18).

phrases.english: Just as with the blood stated regarding inside,

phrases.aramaic: חִיסֵּר אַחַת מִמַּתָּנוֹת לֹא עָשָׂה וְלֹא כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: if he left out one of the placements, he did nothing at all,
so too with the blood stated regarding outside,

phrases.aramaic: חִיסֵּר אַחַת מִמַּתָּנוֹת לֹא עָשָׂה כְּלוּם.
phrases.english: if he left out one of the placements, he did nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges Step 5 with a rival comparison that gives the opposite result.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It does not disprove Step 5. It shows another comparison is just as possible, so the logic of Step 5 is not certain.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bird is not the only possible model. The inner offerings could serve as the model instead.

steps.title: Weighing the comparisons: outside should be learned from outside
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא weighs the two comparisons. It argues that something outside should be learned from something outside, which supports the bird comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let's see which it is more like. We learn outside from outside, and we don't learn outside from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts deciding between the two comparisons and gives a reason to prefer the first one, the bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bird חטאת and the animal חטאת both have their blood placed on the outer מזבח. The inner offerings are placed inside. A comparison between two outside offerings is closer, so this point favors 'one placement is enough'.

keyTerms.meaning: Let's see which it is more like. This begins the weighing of two comparisons.
We learn one case from another.

phrases.english: Let us see which it resembles.
We learn outside from outside,
and we do not learn outside from inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by arguing that the comparison in Step 5 is the closer one.
steps.raayaObject: The comparison to the bird חטאת is better than the comparison to the inner offerings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The idea that an outside offering should be learned from another outside offering.

steps.title: Counter-weighing: learn a four-corner חטאת from another four-corner חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers back that the inner offerings, like the animal חטאת, are placed on four corners, while the bird is not. So the bird cannot be the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or go this way: we learn a חטאת with four corners from a חטאת with four corners. The bird cannot prove anything, because it is not a חטאת with four corners.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against Step 7 with a different point of similarity, so the inner comparison looks stronger again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal חטאת and the inner חטאת both have their blood placed on the four corners of a מזבח. The bird חטאת does not. If the four corners are the key feature, the bird is the weaker model, and the logic ends in a tie.

keyTerms.meaning: The four corners, or horns, of the מזבח, where some offerings' blood is placed.
And let this one not prove. This means that case is too different to serve as a proof.

steps.whatToRemember: Each comparison has its own point of similarity: outside versus inside, or four corners versus not. Since logic can't settle it, the stage is set for a פסוק to decide.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
We learn a sin-offering with four corners
from a sin-offering with four corners,
and let this one not prove,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the bird חטאת from Step 5.

phrases.english: since it is not a sin-offering with four corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ כְּלָךְ לְדֶרֶךְ זוֹ: דָּנִין חַטָּאת וְאַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the weighing in Step 7 by pointing to a different shared feature, which supports Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It cancels the advantage that Step 7 gave to the bird comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The bird חטאת lacks the four-corner placement that the animal חטאת and the inner חטאת share.

steps.title: The three times 'And he shall atone' settle the question
steps.stepSummary: The two logical comparisons cancel each other out, so the ברייתא turns to the verses. Each 'וכפר' teaches that atonement works even with fewer placements of blood: three, then two, then one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'and he shall atone' three times because the logic could go either way. He atones even if he put only three placements, even if only two, and even if only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends its back-and-forth. The logic could not decide the question, so it learns the answer straight from the three times the Torah says 'וכפר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-8 showed that the outer חטאת could be compared to the bird חטאת or to the inner חטאת, and neither comparison won. So the Torah repeats 'וכפר' three times, and each one lowers the minimum: three placements, two, and finally one. This is the source for בית הלל, who say one placement is enough after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches. Used to bring a verse that settles the question.
And he (the כהן) shall atone
Because of the logical argument. The verse is needed because logic could go either way.
He placed (the blood on a corner of the מזבח)

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל's rule, that one placement of blood is enough after the fact, comes from the three times the Torah says 'וכפר'. It does not come from how the word קרנות is read or written.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the answer from Step 4. The argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל no longer proves anything about יש אם למקרא.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And he shall atone,' 'And he shall atone,' 'And he shall atone' because of the logical argument.
phrases.notes: The two comparisons cancelled each other out, so a verse is needed to decide.

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּיפֵּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשָׁה,
phrases.english: 'He atoned' even though he placed only three,

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּיפֵּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: 'He atoned' even though he placed only two,

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּיפֵּר״ – אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן אֶלָּא אַחַת.
phrases.english: 'He atoned' even though he placed only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Logic has reached a dead end, so the ברייתא settles the question with the verses.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One placement of blood is enough after the fact for an outer חטאת. This is learned from the three times the Torah says 'וכפר'.

steps.title: The real argument about סוכה walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון and the רבנן do not argue about יש אם למקרא. They argue about whether the roofing (סכך) needs its own verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about this: רבי שמעון holds that the roofing does not need a verse. The רבנן hold that the roofing needs a verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the סוכה argument in a new way. The argument is not about how the word is read. It is about whether one mention of סוכה is needed to teach the roofing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides can agree on how to count the times the Torah mentions סוכה. רבי שמעון says the roof is obvious and needs no verse, so every mention counts toward walls. The רבנן say one mention is used up teaching the roof, which leaves fewer mentions for walls.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they argue about
The roofing of the סוכה (סכך)
Does not need a verse
He holds / they hold

phrases.english: And רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about this:
phrases.notes: This is the earlier argument about how many walls a סוכה needs.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר, סְכָכָא לָא בָּעֵי קְרָא.
phrases.english: רבי שמעון holds that the roofing does not need a verse.
And the רבנן hold that the roofing does need a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps 2-9 explained the earlier disputes without needing יש אם למסורת. This step does the same for the argument between רבי שמעון and רבנן about סוכה walls.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We first thought רבי שמעון and the רבנן argue about whether the reading or the spelling decides the meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: They both follow the reading. They argue only about whether the roofing needs a verse of its own.

steps.title: The real argument about blood from two dead bodies
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא and the רבנן do not argue about יש אם למקרא either. They argue about what the plural word 'נפשת' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about this: רבי עקיבא holds that 'נפשת' means two. The רבנן hold that 'נפשת' means people in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third argument in a new way. It is about the meaning of the plural word 'נפשת', not about how it is read or written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the plural as 'two bodies'. So blood that came from two dead bodies together can still make a person טמא. The רבנן say the plural just means 'any person', so it teaches nothing about two bodies. Both read the word the same way. They only disagree about what the plural teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Souls or bodies (plural), the word in the verse about טומאת מת
It means two
It means people in general

steps.whatToRemember: Every earlier dispute was explained in another way: the number of judges (רבי and רבנן), the woman who gave birth to a girl (רבי יהודה בן רועץ), the חטאת blood (בית הלל), the סוכה walls, and the blood from two dead bodies. So everyone in them can hold יש אם למקרא. The next step challenges this.

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about this:
phrases.notes: This is the earlier argument about a רביעית of blood that came from two dead bodies.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא holds that 'נפשת' means two,
and the רבנן hold that 'נפשת' means people in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the last of the five earlier opinions that get a new explanation, after רבי and רבנן, רבי יהודה בן רועץ, בית הלל, and the סוכה argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We first thought רבי עקיבא and the רבנן argue about whether the reading or the spelling decides the meaning.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only about whether the plural 'נפשת' means two or means people in general.

steps.title: Does everyone really hold יש אם למקרא? The case of תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that everyone holds יש אם למקרא. It brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל counts four compartments in the head תפילין based on how the word טוטפות is spelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does everyone hold that the reading is what counts? But a ברייתא teaches: 'לטוטפת', 'לטטפת', 'לטוטפות'. Here there are four. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns around and challenges what it just said. It brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל seems to learn the law from how a word is spelled. Step 13 completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just said everyone follows the way a word is read. But רבי ישמעאל counts the three mentions of טוטפות by their spelling. Two are spelled like a singular word and one like a plural, so the plural one counts as two, which makes four. That looks like learning from the spelling (יש אם למסורת), so not everyone seems to agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The way a word is read (with its vowels) is what decides its meaning
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? Used to open a challenge.
The head תפילין
The words (opinion) of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas. יש אם למקרא means you follow how the word is read out loud. יש אם למסורת means you follow how the word is written. רבי ישמעאל seems to count by the writing.

phrases.english: And does everyone hold that the reading is what counts?
But isn't it taught: 'for totefet', 'for totefet', 'for totafot'?
phrases.notes: שמות 13:16, דברים 6:8, דברים 11:18. The first two are spelled like a singular word, and the last like a plural.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי כָּאן אַרְבַּע, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל.
phrases.english: Here there are four. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
phrases.notes: The plural one counts as two, so one plus one plus two makes four compartments.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יֵשׁ אֵם לַמִּקְרָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The answers in Steps 2-11 assumed everyone holds יש אם למקרא. This step challenges that assumption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone holds יש אם למקרא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישמעאל counts the mentions of טוטפות by their spelling to get four compartments. That looks like יש אם למסורת.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's different source for the four compartments
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי עקיבא, who learns 'four' from the meaning of the word טוטפות itself. That leaves רבי ישמעאל relying on how the word is spelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: There is no need for that proof. 'טט' in the Katfi language means two, and 'פת' in the Afriki language means two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it began in step 12. This ending completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not need the spelling, because טוטפות is made of two foreign words that each mean 'two'. Since רבי עקיבא gets the number from the word's meaning, רבי ישמעאל must be learning it from the spelling, which means he holds יש אם למסורת. So not everyone holds יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A word meaning 'two' in the Katfi language
A word meaning 'two' in the Afriki language
It is not needed; there is no need for that proof

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: It is not needed,
phrases.notes: He means there's no need to count letters, because the word טוטפות already means 'four' on its own.

phrases.english: 'tat' in the Katfi language means two,
'pat' in the Afriki language means two.
phrases.notes: Put them together: טט + פת = two plus two = four compartments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 12, which completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone holds יש אם למקרא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא learns 'four' from the word's meaning. So רבי ישמעאל must be learning it from the spelling, which shows he holds יש אם למסורת.

steps.title: They do argue, but only when the reading and the spelling are different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now accepts that the תנאים argue. It limits the argument to cases where the reading and the letters differ. With חלב/חלב the letters are the same, so everyone follows the reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they really do argue. But that is only where the reading differs from the written form. With 'fat' (חֵלֶב) and 'milk' (חֲלֵב), the two are written the same, so everyone holds that the reading is the main authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier idea that everyone agrees. It offers a new answer for the ruling about cooking a young goat in milk.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about יש אם למקרא only begins when the reading pulls one way and the spelling pulls another, as with טוטפות. The letters חלב look exactly the same whether you read 'fat' or 'milk'. Since the spelling gives no other option, everyone follows the reading 'milk'.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, they do argue
The reading (how the word is said) is the main authority
The written form of the word (its letters as spelled)
Fat / milk: the same letters, said differently

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the argument covers every word that can be read in two ways. Here the argument only applies where the spelling itself suggests something different from the reading.

phrases.english: Rather, really they do argue.
But when do these words apply, that they argue?
Where the reading differs from the written form.
But this case of 'fat' and 'milk',
which are like each other (written the same),
the reading is the main authority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of steps 12-13 and gives a new, narrower answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the argument to certain cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone holds יש אם למקרא in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only where the spelling differs from the reading. Where the letters are the same, as with חלב, everyone follows the reading.

steps.title: But 'will see' and 'will be seen' are spelled the same, and they argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. יראה and יראה have identical letters, yet there is still an argument about which reading counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at 'will see' (יִרְאֶה) and 'will be seen' (יֵרָאֶה). They are written the same, and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 14. It is setting up a ברייתא to prove its point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said there is no argument when the letters are the same. Here the same letters can be read 'see' or 'be seen', and someone still learns from the reading that is not used. So the limit from step 14 does not hold.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at; introduces a counter-example
Will see / will be seen: the same letters, said differently

phrases.english: But look at 'will see' and 'will be seen',
which are like each other (written the same), and they argue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set up in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no one argues when the letters are the same
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יראה/יראה are spelled the same, and an argument still exists.

steps.title: Someone blind in one eye is exempt from appearing in the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of יוחנן בן דהבאי learns from the reading 'will see' that a person must be able to see with both eyes in order to be obligated to appear in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: יוחנן בן דהבאי says in the name of רבי יהודה בן תימא: Someone blind in one of his eyes is exempt from appearing in the בית המקדש. This is because the פסוק can be read 'will see' or 'will be seen'. Just as he comes to see, so he comes to be seen. Just as seeing is done with both eyes, so being seen requires both eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves the challenge from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way we read the פסוק is 'will be seen' (appear). But this ברייתא also learns from the other possible reading, 'will see'. Since he learns from the reading we do not use, even with identical letters, the claim that everyone follows the reading here is disproved.

keyTerms.meaning: A blind person
The מצוה of appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים
Exempt; not obligated
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Yochanan ben Dahavai says
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda ben Teima:
One who is blind in one of his eyes
is exempt from the מצוה of appearing,
phrases.notes: This is the מצוה to come and be seen in the בית המקדש on the three רגלים.

phrases.english: as it says 'will see' / 'will be seen',
In the same way that he comes to see,
so he comes to be seen.
Just as seeing is with both his eyes,
so too being seen is with both his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source that backs up the challenge in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That people argue even when the letters are the same
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of יוחנן בן דהבאי in the name of רבי יהודה בן תימא, which learns from the reading 'will see'

steps.title: The Torah forbade the normal way of cooking
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא explains the milk ruling without relying on יש אם למקרא. 'Do not cook' means normal cooking, and normal cooking is done in a liquid like milk, not in fat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אחא son of רב איקא said: The פסוק says 'Do not cook a young goat.' The Torah forbade the normal way of cooking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new and final reason why everyone agrees the prohibition is about milk and not fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof no longer comes from how the word חלב is read. It comes from the word 'cook' (תבשל). Cooking is normally done in a liquid, and fat is not a cooking liquid. So the prohibition must be about milk, whatever one holds about יש אם למקרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says; introduces a proof from a פסוק
Do not cook a young goat
The normal way of cooking

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees בשר בחלב is about milk. The reason is not how חלב is read, but that 'cooking' normally means cooking in a liquid.
steps.whyThisMatters: It takes the milk ruling out of the יש אם למקרא argument altogether. That keeps the argument between the תנאים intact.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
The פסוק says: 'Do not cook a young goat,'
the Torah forbade the normal way of cooking.
phrases.notes: Normal cooking is done in a liquid like milk, not in solid fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops the answer from step 14 after the challenge in steps 15-16 and gives a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source from the meaning of the word 'cook'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees on milk because the letters חלב are spelled the same either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees on milk because 'cooking' normally means cooking in a liquid.

steps.title: A ברייתא: monetary cases need three judges
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא stating that דיני ממונות are judged by a court of three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught in a ברייתא: monetary cases are judged by three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a new ברייתא. This is the opening line, and it sets up what the ברייתא will say next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line of the ברייתא gives the basic rule that a monetary case needs a בית דין of three. The ברייתא is not finished here. It continues in the next lines, which build on this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "The רבנן taught." This phrase opens a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself.
Monetary cases, such as loans, damages, and other disputes over money.
By three judges.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Monetary cases are judged by three,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אחא בריה דרב איקא's answer about the milk ruling, the גמרא turns to quote a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Monetary cases are judged by a court of three judges.
